summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute a 727KB obfuscated payload
details: @servicetitan/datadog-rum@38.1.5 ships a preinstall hook (`preinstall: node setup.mjs` in package.json) that downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases, extracts it, chmods it executable, and then invokes the freshly-fetched Bun binary against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727,680-byte single-line file whose content is heavily obfuscated: hex-named identifiers (`MmgoCP`, `_0x...`), a shuffled string-array rotation function (`WV8StW`) that repeatedly shifts/pushes ~1000 mixed integer/string entries, and only the `@bun @bun-cjs` header is human-readable. The package's stated purpose is a Datadog RUM wrapper — nothing in that purpose requires downloading a second language runtime at install time, and running the payload through an alternate runtime evades Node-only inspection. The scope `@servicetitan/*` is not owned by ServiceTitan on npm in a way that reconciles with this shipped content, matching the vendor-scope-impersonation pattern used in recent npm supply-chain worm activity. Installing the package causes an alternate-runtime-dropper payload to execute arbitrary code with the installing user's privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
